papers.title_zh: 泰国5岁儿童中预暴露预防狂犬病 疫苗的成本效用分析。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Rabies remains a life-threatening disease affecting children in endemic regions including Thailand. The cost-effectiveness of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) rabies vaccination in the Thai context is unclear. This study analysed the cost-utility of adding PrEP rabies vaccination to post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) rabies vaccination compared with PEP alone in 5-year-old children. METHODS: A decision tree model compared eight strategies (four PEP alone and four PrEP+PEP), classified by route of administration (intradermal (ID) or intramuscular (IM)) and vaccine product (purified chick embryo cell vaccine (PCEC) or chromatographically purified Vero cell vaccine (CPRV)/purified Vero cell rabies vaccine (PVRV)). Costs and outcomes were derived from published literature and discounted at 3% annually. The analysis was conducted from a societal perspective over a 20-year horizon. Incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) were evaluated against Thailand's willingness-to-pay threshold of THB 160 000 per quality-adjusted life year (QALY). RESULTS: PrEP+PEP ID using PCEC was cost-effective, with an ICER of THB 40 977 (US$1160.8) per QALY versus PEP alone ID using PCEC; the remaining strategies were dominated. The one-way sensitivity analysis identified annual bite incidence as the most influential parameter, with the ICER ranging from cost-saving to not cost-effective (THB 454 265 (US$12 868.7) per QALY). The results were robust to variation in all other parameters. CONCLUSION: PrEP+PEP ID using PCEC is cost-effective for children in Thailand, reducing reliance on equine rabies immunoglobulin and disease-related QALY losses. These findings support integrating PrEP into Thailand's National Immunization Program for children in high-risk areas, prioritising early vaccination in high-risk populations to advance the goal of eliminating rabies by 2030.
papers.abstract_zh: 引言:狂犬病仍然是威胁儿童生命的疾病,包括泰国在内的流行地区均受影响。在泰国背景下,预暴露预防(PrEP)狂犬病 疫苗接种的成本效益尚不明确。本研究分析了在5岁儿童中,将PrEP 狂犬病 疫苗接种与暴露后预防(暴露后预防,PEP)狂犬病 疫苗接种联合使用与单独使用PEP的成本效用。方法:采用决策树模型比较了八种策略(四种单独使用PEP和四种联合使用PrEP+PEP),根据给药途径(皮内(ID)或肌肉内(IM))和疫苗产品(纯化鸡胚胎细胞疫苗(PCEC)或色谱纯化的Vero细胞疫苗(CPRV)/纯化的Vero细胞狂犬病 疫苗(PVRV))进行分类。成本和结果来源于已发表的文献,并按每年3%的折现率进行折现。分析从社会视角出发,时间跨度为20年。增量成本效用比(ICERs)以泰国每质量调整生命年(QALY)160 000泰铢的意愿支付阈值为基准进行评估。结果:使用PCEC的PrEP+PEP ID策略具有成本效益,其ICER为每QALY 40 977泰铢(约合1160.8美元),相较于单独使用PEP ID的PCEC策略;其余策略均被判定为占优策略。单向敏感性分析显示,每年咬伤次数发病率是影响最大的参数,ICER范围从成本节约到不具成本效益(每QALY 454 265泰铢(约合12 868.7美元))。结果对其他参数的变化具有稳健性。结论:使用PCEC的PrEP+PEP ID策略在泰国儿童中具有成本效益,可减少对马源狂犬病免疫球蛋白的依赖,并降低与疾病相关的QALY损失。这些发现支持将PrEP纳入泰国国家免疫计划,以在高风险地区儿童中实现消除狂犬病的目标。科学意义与公共卫生意义:这些发现支持将PrEP纳入泰国国家免疫计划,优先在高风险人群中进行早期疫苗接种接种,以推进到2030年消除狂犬病的目标。局限性与证据强度:分析基于已发表的文献,可能受到源研究中假设和数据的限制。证据强度中等,因为它依赖于现有数据而非原创研究。

papers.title: 5’ untranslated region (5’ UTR) of bovine β-globin in the mRNA constructs translates different types of antigenic proteins
papers.abstract: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5’UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5’UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5’UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5’UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5’UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5’UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for an ideal 5’UTR that supports higher translation efficiency for different antigens, as natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA. This is critical for the development of next-generation mRNA vaccine platforms.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The translation efficiency was assessed in different cell lines.
analysis.methods: The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription, and translation efficiency was evaluated using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments.
analysis.main_results: The results revealed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins across different cell lines. Additionally, it supported the expression of various antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR can be effectively used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases, highlighting its versatility in supporting translation of different antigenic proteins.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective mRNA vaccines for animal diseases, particularly those targeting rabies virus and related pathogens, by providing a reliable 5’UTR that enhances translation efficiency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the potential of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR as a universal mRNA translation enhancer for different antigens. The research aimed to address the challenge of finding an effective 5’UTR for mRNA vaccine development, as natural 5’UTRs are gene-specific. The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs upstream to reporter proteins and assessing their translation efficiency in vitro. Results showed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly enhanced translation across various cell lines and supported the expression of different antigenic proteins, including rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), foot and mouth disease virus (VP1), and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR could be used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases. The study's in vitro nature limits its generalizability, but the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the 5’UTR. These findings have implications for improving mRNA vaccine platforms for animal diseases, particularly rabies.

elements_zh.methods: 通过体外转录生成相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和Western blot实验评估翻译效率。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR显著提高了报告蛋白在不同细胞系中的翻译效率。此外,它还支持多种抗原蛋白的表达,如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒的主要结构蛋白(VP1)以及细菌epsilon毒素蛋白(Eptx)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR可以有效地用于针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗设计的证据,突出了其在支持不同抗原蛋白翻译方面的多功能性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发更有效的针对动物疾病的mRNA 疫苗提供信息,特别是针对狂犬病病毒及相关病原体的疫苗,通过提供一种可靠的5’UTR来增强翻译效率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于体外评估,未包括体内验证,这可能会影响研究结果的普遍适用性。然而,结果得到了多种实验方法的支持,对牛β-珠蛋白5’UTR有效性的信心中等。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for an ideal 5’UTR that supports higher translation efficiency for different antigens, as natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA. This is critical for the development of next-generation mRNA vaccine platforms.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study involved cloning six natural 5’UTRs from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The translation efficiency was assessed in different cell lines.
analysis_en.methods: The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription, and translation efficiency was evaluated using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments.
analysis_en.main_results: The results revealed that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR significantly increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins across different cell lines. Additionally, it supported the expression of various antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx).
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the bovine β-globin 5’UTR can be effectively used in mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases, highlighting its versatility in supporting translation of different antigenic proteins.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the development of more effective mRNA vaccines for animal diseases, particularly those targeting rabies virus and related pathogens, by providing a reliable 5’UTR that enhances translation efficiency.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to in vitro assessments and does not include in vivo validation, which may affect the generalizability of the findings. However, the results are supported by multiple experimental methods, providing moderate confidence in the effectiveness of the bovine β-globin 5’UTR.

papers.title_zh: mRNA 构建体中牛 β-珠蛋白的 5' 非翻译区 (5' UTR) 可翻译不同类型的抗原蛋白
papers.source_body_en: Synthetic messenger RNA (mRNA) is emerging as next generation vaccine platform. As natural 5’UTRs of particular genes do not work for other than its own mRNA, it is essential to identify an ideal 5’UTR supporting higher translation efficiency for different antigens. Six natural 5’UTRs derived from α, β-globin genes of host animals and other viral genes were cloned upstream to the coding sequences of reporter proteins. The corresponding capped mRNA were produced through in vitro transcription and the translation efficiency was assessed using flow cytometry, bioluminescence, immunofluorescence and western blot experiments. The results revealed higher translation of reporter proteins by bovine β-globin 5’UTR in different cell lines. Further, the chosen 5’UTR supported mRNA translation to produce different antigenic proteins such as rabies virus glycoprotein (RVG), major structural protein of foot and mouth disease virus (VP1) and bacterial epsilon toxoid protein (Eptx). Bovine -globin 5’UTR not only increased the translation efficiency of reporter proteins but also supported the expression of different antigenic proteins. Hence, bovine -globin 5’UTR can be used in the mRNA vaccine designs against animal diseases.
papers.abstract_zh: 合成信使 RNA (mRNA) 正在成为下一代 疫苗 平台。由于特定基因的天然 5'UTR 只能作用于其自身的 mRNA,因此有必要确定一个理想的 5'UTR,以支持不同抗原的更高翻译效率。来自 宿主 动物的 α、β-球蛋白基因和其他病毒基因的 6 个天然 5'UTR 被克隆到报告蛋白编码序列的上游。通过体外转录产生相应的加帽mRNA,并使用流式细胞术、生物发光、免疫荧光和蛋白质印迹实验评估翻译效率。结果表明,牛 β-珠蛋白 5'UTR 在不同细胞系中对报告蛋白的翻译更高。此外,所选的5'UTR支持mRNA翻译以产生不同的抗原蛋白,例如狂犬病病毒糖蛋白(RVG)、口蹄疫病毒(VP1)的主要结构蛋白和细菌ε类毒素蛋白(Eptx)。牛珠蛋白5'UTR不仅提高了报告蛋白的翻译效率,而且支持不同抗原蛋白的表达。因此,牛珠蛋白 5'UTR 可用于针对动物疾病的 mRNA 疫苗 设计。

papers.title: Potential for real-time health and welfare monitoring of red fox (Vulpes vulpes) in experimental settings using implants
papers.abstract: Monitoring and improving animal health and welfare is a pressing need. Technological advances are increasing our ability to do so in a range of settings but there are limited uses in experimental settings for less common model animals. Red foxes ( Vulpes vulpes ) are maintained by the French National Agency for Food, Environmental, and Occupational Health and Safety (ANSES) for regulatory and research purposes, primarily related to its role as a European Union and French Reference Laboratory for rabies and Echinococcus spp., both serious zoonoses. In 2022, four foxes were surgically fitted with internal implants that recorded body temperature and activity levels and subsequently inoculated with rabies virus (RABV). As a proof of concept, we retrospectively tested the potential of these two variables to provide an early warning for the onset of rabies symptoms. To do so, we applied two anomaly detection algorithms (Shewhart and EWMA) with varying confidence levels individually to the two data sets from each fox and compared how early the different models could detect significant changes while limiting false alarms during the calibration period. We found that all the foxes significantly changed their activity during infection. We were best able to detect these changes at the individual fox level using the EWMA algorithm, in some cases producing consecutive alarms up to two weeks before the death of an animal, while limiting false alarms. We found no evidence of fever in any of the infected foxes and body temperature did not appear to be a reliable indicator of foxes’ health in this context. While here we applied our methods to a particularly severe and rarely implemented model with a limited sample size, this proof of concept illustrates the potential of these methods for a wide range of other situations that would benefit from similar long-term monitoring, including experimental protocols with milder clinical signs and routine monitoring for unexpected declines in health or welfare.

As a proof of concept, we retrospectively tested the potential of these two variables to provide an early warning for the onset of rabies symptoms. To do so, we applied two anomaly detection algorithms (Shewhart and EWMA) with varying confidence levels individually to the two data sets from each fox and compared how early the different models could detect significant changes while limiting false alarms during the calibration period. We found that all the foxes significantly changed their activity during infection. We were best able to detect these changes at the individual fox level using the EWMA algorithm, in some cases producing consecutive alarms up to two weeks before the death of an animal, while limiting false alarms. We found no evidence of fever in any of the infected foxes and body temperature did not appear to be a reliable indicator of foxes’ health in this context. While here we applied our methods to a particularly severe and rarely implemented model with a limited sample size, this proof of concept illustrates the potential of these methods for a wide range of other situations that would benefit from similar long-term monitoring, including experimental protocols with milder clinical signs and routine monitoring for unexpected declines in health or welfare.

papers.title: EPIDEMIOLOGICAL PROFILE OF COMPULSORY NOTIFICATIONS OF HUMAN ANTIRABIES CARE IN PORTO NACIONAL, TOCANTINS, BRAZIL
papers.abstract: This study aimed to analyze the epidemiological profile of compulsory notifications related to human anti-rabies care in the municipality of Porto Nacional, Tocantins, Brazil, from 2015 to 2025. This was an observational, descriptive, retrospective, quantitative, and censusbased study using notification data provided by the Municipal Health Surveillance Department. A total of 5,813 records were analyzed, considering sociodemographic variables, characteristics of exposure, prophylactic management, number of recorded vaccine doses, and temporal distribution. The results showed a predominance of males, individuals aged 1 to 19 years, and residents of urban areas. Bites were the main type of exposure, with dogs being the animals most frequently involved. Lower limbs, hands, and feet showed the highest frequencies regarding injury location. Animal observation was the most frequently recommended management, and a high frequency of records without registered vaccine doses was observed. The temporal distribution showed fluctuations, with an increase in attendances during the final years of the study period and the highest number of records in 2025. It is concluded that these findings may support surveillance, prevention, and health education actions.

The research addressed the need for understanding the patterns and characteristics of rabies exposure and management in a specific region to inform public health interventions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was an observational, descriptive, retrospective, quantitative, and census-based study using notification data provided by the Municipal Health Surveillance Department. The study covered a period from 2015 to 2025 and included 5,813 records.
analysis.methods: A total of 5,813 records were analyzed, considering sociodemographic variables, characteristics of exposure, prophylactic management, number of recorded vaccine doses, and temporal distribution.
analysis.main_results: The results showed a predominance of males, individuals aged 1 to 19 years, and residents of urban areas. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors concluded that these findings may support surveillance, prevention, and health education actions. The study highlighted the importance of understanding the epidemiological profile to tailor interventions effectively.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform surveillance, prevention, and health education actions to reduce the incidence of rabies in the region. Understanding the patterns of exposure and management can help in designing targeted public health interventions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在分析2015年至2025年间巴西托坎廷斯州葡萄牙纳尔市与人类抗狂犬病护理相关的强制报告的流行病学特征。研究旨在了解特定地区狂犬病暴露和管理的模式和特征,以指导公共卫生干预措施。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是一项观察性、描述性、回顾性、定量且基于普查的研究,使用了市卫生监测部门提供的报告数据。研究时间跨度为2015年至2025年,共纳入5,813份记录。
elements_zh.methods: 共分析了5,813份记录,考虑了社会人口学变量、暴露特征、预防性管理、记录的疫苗剂量数量以及时间分布。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果显示男性占主导地位,1至19岁的人群以及城市居民占比较高。咬伤是主要的暴露类型,狗是最常涉及的动物。下肢、手和脚在受伤部位中出现频率最高。时间分布显示出波动,研究期间最后几年的就诊次数增加,2025年的记录数量最高。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者得出结论,这些发现可能支持监测、预防和健康教育行动。该研究强调了了解流行病学特征以有效制定干预措施的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为监测、预防和健康教育行动提供信息,以减少该地区发病率的发生。了解暴露和管理的模式有助于设计针对性的公共卫生干预措施。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受限于其依赖于报告数据,可能无法涵盖所有狂犬病暴露病例。大量未记录疫苗剂量的记录表明预防性管理可能存在缺口。由于研究的观察性质以及可能的漏报,证据强度中等。

It is concluded that these findings may support surveillance, prevention, and health education actions.

papers.title: Responsible Ownership and Welfare Indicators for Dogs and Cats in Rural Lithuania: Self-Reported Practices and In-Person Assessment
papers.abstract: Dogs and cats are increasingly regarded as companion animals and family members, but companionship requires more than affection: it also entails responsibility for their health, reproduction, housing and behavioural needs. Responsible ownership and welfare in rural Baltic and Eastern European settings remain poorly studied. The study included 383 Lithuanian owners (338 rural, 45 urban) and welfare assessments of 85 animals from 53 rural households using an adapted Animal Welfare Assessment Grid. Animal numbers per household differed significantly by residence (p = 0.0008), with 73.1% of rural respondents keeping two or more animals versus 46.7% of urban respondents. Microchipping of all household animals was less often reported by rural than urban respondents (55.5% vs. 86.7%; p = 0.0003), as was rabies vaccination within the previous three years (67.1% vs. Neutering of all animals was likewise less common in rural households, although not significantly (50.6% vs. Main welfare concerns were environmental enrichment, body condition, frequency of exposure to stressors, behaviour during procedures and the living environment; older animals had poorer scores (p = 0.0004). Rural households kept more animals, while several responsible ownership practices were less consistently implemented, potentially amplifying welfare and population-management consequences and supporting rural education and preventive veterinary initiatives.

papers.title_zh: 农村立陶宛犬猫负责任的饲养与福利指标:自我报告的实践与实地评估
papers.source_body_en: Dogs and cats are increasingly regarded as companion animals and family members, but companionship requires more than affection: it also entails responsibility for their health, reproduction, housing and behavioural needs. Responsible ownership and welfare in rural Baltic and Eastern European settings remain poorly studied. The study included 383 Lithuanian owners (338 rural, 45 urban) and welfare assessments of 85 animals from 53 rural households using an adapted Animal Welfare Assessment Grid. Animal numbers per household differed significantly by residence (p = 0.0008), with 73.1% of rural respondents keeping two or more animals versus 46.7% of urban respondents. Microchipping of all household animals was less often reported by rural than urban respondents (55.5% vs. 86.7%; p = 0.0003), as was rabies vaccination within the previous three years (67.1% vs. Neutering of all animals was likewise less common in rural households, although not significantly (50.6% vs. Main welfare concerns were environmental enrichment, body condition, frequency of exposure to stressors, behaviour during procedures and the living environment; older animals had poorer scores (p = 0.0004). Rural households kept more animals, while several responsible ownership practices were less consistently implemented, potentially amplifying welfare and population-management consequences and supporting rural education and preventive veterinary initiatives.
papers.abstract_zh: 犬和猫正日益被视为伴侣动物和家庭成员,但陪伴不仅仅需要关爱:它还涉及对其健康、繁殖、居住和行为需求的责任。在农村波罗的海和东欧地区,负责任的饲养和动物福利状况仍缺乏充分研究。本研究纳入了383名立陶宛饲养者(338名农村,45名城市),并使用改良的动物福利评估网格对53个农村家庭中的85只动物进行了福利评估。每户饲养的动物数量在居住地类型上存在显著差异(p = 0.0008),其中73.1%的农村受访者饲养两只或更多动物,而城市受访者中这一比例为46.7%。所有家庭动物的微芯片植入在农村受访者中报告较少(55.5% vs. 86.7%;p = 0.0003),在过去的三年内进行绝育的比例也较低(67.1% vs. 所有动物的绝育在农村家庭中同样较少,但未达到显著差异(50.6% vs. 主要的福利问题包括环境丰富度、身体状况、接触压力源的频率、程序期间的行为以及生活环境;老年动物的评分较差(p = 0.0004)。农村家庭饲养的动物更多,而一些负责任的饲养实践实施得不够一致,这可能加剧动物福利和种群管理方面的后果,并支持农村地区的教育和预防兽医倡议。

The incident underscores the importance of immediate response to prevent rabies transmission. While the event is reported as a single case, no broader outbreak or public health risk is indicated. The WHO's focus is on raising awareness and promoting preventive measures rather than detailing specific investigation or containment efforts. This case serves as a reminder of the critical need for timely medical intervention following animal bites, especially in regions where rabies remains a significant health threat. The response is part of WHO's broader campaigns to educate the public on rabies prevention and control.

news.source_body_en: The World Health Organization (WHO) highlighted a Vietnamese student's quick action after a dog bite as part of its World Rabies Day activities. The incident underscores the importance of immediate response to prevent rabies transmission. While the event is reported as a single case, no broader outbreak or public health risk is indicated. The WHO's focus is on raising awareness and promoting preventive measures rather than detailing specific investigation or containment efforts. This case serves as a reminder of the critical need for timely medical intervention following animal bites, especially in regions where rabies remains a significant health threat. news.content_zh: 世界卫生组织(WHO)在世界狂犬病日活动中强调了一位越南学生在犬咬伤后迅速应对的案例。该事件突显了及时应对以防止狂犬病 传播的重要性。尽管该事件被报告为单一案例,但并未表明存在更广泛的暴发或公共卫生风险。WHO的重点在于提高公众意识并推广预防措施,而不是详细说明特定的调查或控制措施。这一案例提醒人们,在犬咬伤后及时进行医疗干预至关重要,尤其是在狂犬病仍是重要健康威胁的地区。该回应是WHO更广泛宣传活动的一部分,旨在向公众普及狂犬病的预防和控制知识。

Email Us Emergencies Support Us Breadcrumb CVM About Us News Two confirmed cases of rabies in a New York beef herd Friday, September 25, 2026 - 12:19pm In September 2026, over the course of three weeks, three adult Angus beef cattle in a herd of 114 animals developed severe acute neurologic signs and died. Clinical signs included excessive salivation and vocalization, absent gaze, running through fences and gates and severe pruritus, leading to self-trauma and skin damage. The owner thought the first animal, a bull, had an esophageal obstruction (commonly referred to as “choke”). The owner passed an orogastric tube to relieve the possible obstruction, but the bull died within hours. The second and third animals (adult cows) became neurologic and died. The owner contacted the herd veterinarian, who collected the appropriate brain sample for rabies testing in both animals. This included a full cross section of the cerebellum and a section of brainstem. The fresh sample must be placed in a sterile container and sent for overnight delivery with ice packs to the New York State Department of Health, Wadsworth Center in Albany, NY. Additionally, formalin fixed tissues and fresh tissues from the third cow were submitted to the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center (AHDC) for histopathology and ancillary testing. A top differential based on the neurologic clinical signs in pasture-based cattle was lead toxicosis. Lead testing on fresh liver tissue was negative. Fluorescent antibody staining for rabies was positive in both cows. Histopathology of the brain performed at the AHDC revealed intraneuronal intracytoplasmic viral inclusion bodies (Negri bodies),1 which is pathognomonic lesion for rabies virus (Image 1). An immunohistochemical stain for rabies was applied to the histology slides as well, staining the Negri bodies a dark red (Image 2). Rabies virus is a negative sense RNA virus in the lyssavirus genus, Rhabdoviridae family.1 It is zoonotic and causes encephalitis due to neurotropism. It is almost 100% fatal. Rabies is reportable and preventable by vaccination. The remaining cattle on the premise and a single horse were vaccinated for rabies by the herd veterinarian. The exposed farmer was administered post-exposure prophylaxis. In this case, the veterinarian submitted brain samples directly to the Wadsworth laboratory. The AHDC necropsy laboratory can perform brain extraction on rabies suspect animals from New York and submit the sample to the Wadsworth Center Rabies Laboratory for practitioners as well. Submitting veterinarians must fill out an animal rabies specimen history form in addition to the AHDC submission form. This form accompanies the cerebellum and brainstem samples to the Wadsworth Center Rabies Laboratory. Image 1: Histologic examination of the brain of cow 3 reveals a mild meningoencephalitis. White arrows point to intraneuronal intracytoplasmic viral inclusion bodies, called Negri bodies. 3 (white arrows). Image 2: Histologic examination of the brain of cow 3 with an immunohistochemistry staining Negri bodies a dark red (white arrows). Reference Lahaye X, Vidy A, Pomier C, Obiang L, Harper F, Gaudin Y, Blondel D. Functional characterization of Negri bodies (NBs) in rabies virus-infected cells: Evidence that NBs are sites of viral transcription and replication. J Virol. 2009 Aug;83(16):7948-58. doi: 10.1128/JVI.00554-09. Epub 2009 Jun 3. PMID: 19494013; PMCID: PMC2715764. analysis.time: In September 2026, over the course of three weeks, three adult Angus beef cattle in a herd of 114 animals developed severe acute neurologic signs and died. The publication date is 2026-09-25.
analysis.location_and_population: The event occurred in a New York beef herd, specifically in Ithaca, NY, involving 114 cattle and a single horse.
analysis.event: Two confirmed cases of rabies were identified in a New York beef herd. The owner initially suspected an esophageal obstruction in the first animal, but rabies was confirmed through fluorescent antibody staining and histopathology. The event was reported by Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Three adult cattle died due to rabies. The remaining cattle and a single horse were vaccinated. The exposed farmer received post-exposure prophylaxis. Rabies is almost 100% fatal and is a zoonotic disease that causes encephalitis due to neurotropism.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The veterinarian collected brain samples for rabies testing, submitted them to the New York State Department of Health, Wadsworth Center, and the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center. The samples were tested using fluorescent antibody staining and histopathology. The response included vaccination of the remaining cattle and a horse, and post-exposure prophylaxis for the exposed farmer.

analysis.brief_en: In September 2026, three adult Angus cattle in a herd of 114 animals in New York developed severe acute neurologic signs and died. The Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine confirmed two cases of rabies through fluorescent antibody staining and histopathology, which revealed intraneuronal viral inclusion bodies (Negri bodies). The owner initially suspected an esophageal obstruction in the first animal but later submitted brain samples for testing. The remaining cattle and a single horse were vaccinated, and the exposed farmer received post-exposure prophylaxis. Rabies, a zoonotic disease caused by the rabies virus, is almost 100% fatal and leads to encephalitis due to its neurotropism. The samples were sent to the New York State Department of Health, Wadsworth Center, and the Cornell Animal Health Diagnostic Center for further analysis. The event highlights the importance of rabies testing and prevention measures in livestock.

news.content_zh: 2026年9月,纽约一个拥有114头牛的牛群中,三头成年安格斯牛出现了严重的急性神经症状并死亡。康奈尔大学兽医学院通过荧光抗体染色和组织病理学确认了两例狂犬病病例,观察到神经元内病毒包涵体(Negri bodies)。最初,牛主怀疑第一头牛患有食管阻塞,但随后提交了脑组织样本进行检测。其余的牛和一匹马接受了疫苗接种,暴露的农民接受了暴露后预防。狂犬病是一种由狂犬病病毒引起的、几乎100%致命的人兽共患病,由于其神经嗜性导致脑炎。样本被送往纽约州卫生部瓦德斯沃斯中心和康奈尔动物健康诊断中心进行进一步分析。该事件突显了在畜牧业中进行狂犬病检测和预防措施的重要性。

Conditions Los Angeles County Nears Its Rabid Bat Record with 66 Detections as California Tallies 252 Animal Rabies Cases Published Sep 22, 2026 7:30 AM EDT By Joseph James MENAHEM KAHANA | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Los Angeles County has confirmed 66 rabid bats so far this year, two short of its all-time high of 68 set in 2021, according to the county Department of Public Health's 2026 rabies map, last updated Sept. 21. Statewide, California counted 252 rabid animals from Jan. 1 through Aug. 31, including 232 bats, 19 skunks, and one dog, according to provisional figures from the California Department of Public Health's animal rabies table that were reported by KCLU. These are animal cases, not human ones. The risk that matters for households is exposure. In Los Angeles County, most rabid bats this year turned up where families live, including backyards, driveways, pools, and patios, and in several cases inside homes, often with a dog or cat nearby. A single unnoticed contact can lead to a costly series of shots for a person and strict follow-up measures for an unvaccinated pet. A Statewide Count Nearing a Full Year's Total in Eight Months The 252 animals counted through August nearly match the 254 rabid animals California reported for all of 2024 and exceed the 202 reported for all of 2023, according to CDPH's final tables for those years. The 2026 figure is provisional and could change. Timing makes the number more notable. Rabid bat reports in California typically peak from summer into early fall, and September and October detections are not yet included in the statewide total. Higher counts can also reflect more testing, because the bats that reach labs are ones that people found and reported. Neighboring Ventura County has confirmed 27 rabid bats this year, a county record, up from 22 last year and six the year before. "We don't know why this increase is happening," said Randy Friedman of Ventura County Animal Services. Santa Clarita at the Center of Los Angeles County's Detections The county's detailed list shows about two-thirds of this year's rabid bats came from the Santa Clarita Valley, including Valencia, Newhall, Canyon Country, Castaic, and Stevenson Ranch. Others were found in Burbank, Glendale, Calabasas, Woodland Hills, Tarzana, Glendora, Monrovia, and several Los Angeles neighborhoods. The entries read like a household checklist. Bats were found in swimming pools, tucked between patio furniture cushions, on front porches, inside a bedroom and a living room, and in the mouths of dogs. At least three exposures involved cats or dogs that were not up to date on rabies vaccines, the list shows. When the county reported a near-record count last year, Los Angeles County Health Officer Dr. Muntu Davis put the core message simply: "Never touch a bat or any wild animals." The county's rabies guidance asks residents to report any bat found indoors, or any bat outdoors that appears sick, is active during the day, cannot fly, or is dead. Treatment Demand and Costs Are Rising Nationally California's numbers arrive as federal health officials warn of a national increase in human rabies exposures. In a Sept. 10 health advisory, the CDC said it received 17% more rabies-related inquiries in July and August than during the same period a year earlier. Use of rabies vaccines rose an estimated 33%, and use of rabies immune globulin rose 76%. The agency said there is currently no shortage. MedicalDaily covered the advisory's warning about treatment errors. Post-exposure treatment prevents rabies when it is given appropriately before symptoms start, but it is expensive. A typical course costs $11,000 to $14,000 per person, according to the CDC. That is why a risk assessment matters. The CDC says treatment generally is not recommended when the animal can be observed for 10 days, tests negative, or officials determine there was no rabies risk. For bats, testing is often the deciding factor. If it can be done safely, the bat should be contained rather than released so animal control can test it. Local health departments can help families weigh the risk, and patients can ask their insurer how post-exposure treatment is covered. Steps to Take After Finding a Bat at Home Do not touch a bat with bare hands, and keep children and pets away. If someone was bitten or scratched, or a bat's saliva may have reached the eyes, nose, mouth, or a wound, wash the area with soap and water for 15 minutes and contact a clinician or the local health department right away. Bat bites can be tiny, so waking up with a bat in the room or finding one near a sleeping child should be treated as a possible exposure, according to Los Angeles County officials. Keep dogs and cats current on rabies vaccines, including indoor pets, since the county notes that at least one rabid bat is found indoors every year. Seal gaps where bats can get into attics and living spaces. Rabies symptoms in people can take weeks to months to appear and may begin like the flu, with fever and headache, before progressing to neurological problems. Once symptoms start, the disease is almost always fatal, which is why officials urge prompt evaluation instead of waiting. The risk to any one Californian remains low, and the numbers call for vigilance rather than panic. Los Angeles County updates its map as new bats test positive, and MedicalDaily will follow whether the county breaks its 2021 record this fall. Provisional state data count 252 rabid animals from Jan. 1 through Aug. 31, including 232 bats, 19 skunks, and one dog. These are animal cases, not human cases. Why are more rabid bats being found? Officials do not know for certain. Ventura County's animal services said the cause of its increase is unclear, and higher counts can also reflect more bats being found and tested. How many rabid bats has Los Angeles County found? The county had confirmed 66 rabid bats as of its Sept. 21 update, two short of the record 68 set in 2021. About two-thirds were in the Santa Clarita Valley. What counts as a rabies exposure from a bat? A bite, a scratch, or saliva reaching the eyes, nose, mouth, or a wound. Waking up with a bat in the room or finding one near a sleeping child is treated as a possible exposure. What should I do if I find a bat at home? Do not touch it, keep people and pets away, and call animal control. If contact may have occurred, wash the area for 15 minutes and contact a clinician or the health department. Conditions Los Angeles County Nears Its Rabid Bat Record with 66 Detections as California Tallies 252 Animal Rabies Cases Published Sep 22, 2026 7:30 AM EDT By Joseph James MENAHEM KAHANA | AFP via Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on Pocket Los Angeles County has confirmed 66 rabid bats so far this year, two short of its all-time high of 68 set in 2021, according to the county Department of Public Health's 2026 rabies map, last updated Sept. 21. Statewide, California counted 252 rabid animals from Jan. 1 through Aug. 31, including 232 bats, 19 skunks, and one dog, according to provisional figures from the California Department of Public Health's animal rabies table that were reported by KCLU. These are animal cases, not human ones. The risk that matters for households is exposure. In Los Angeles County, most rabid bats this year turned up where families live, including backyards, driveways, pools, and patios, and in several cases inside homes, often with a dog or cat nearby. A single unnoticed contact can lead to a costly series of shots for a person and strict follow-up measures for an unvaccinated pet. A Statewide Count Nearing a Full Year's Total in Eight Months The 252 animals counted through August nearly match the 254 rabid animals California reported for all of 2024 and exceed the 202 reported for all of 2023, according to CDPH's final tables for those years. The 2026 figure is provisional and could change. Timing makes the number more notable. Rabid bat reports in California typically peak from summer into early fall, and September and October detections are not yet included in the statewide total. Higher counts can also reflect more testing, because the bats that reach labs are ones that people found and reported. Neighboring Ventura County has confirmed 27 rabid bats this year, a county record, up from 22 last year and six the year before. "We don't know why this increase is happening," said Randy Friedman of Ventura County Animal Services. Santa Clarita at the Center of Los Angeles County's Detections The county's detailed list shows about two-thirds of this year's rabid bats came from the Santa Clarita Valley, including Valencia, Newhall, Canyon Country, Castaic, and Stevenson Ranch. Others were found in Burbank, Glendale, Calabasas, Woodland Hills, Tarzana, Glendora, Monrovia, and several Los Angeles neighborhoods. The entries read like a household checklist. Bats were found in swimming pools, tucked between patio furniture cushions, on front porches, inside a bedroom and a living room, and in the mouths of dogs. At least three exposures involved cats or dogs that were not up to date on rabies vaccines, the list shows. When the county reported a near-record count last year, Los Angeles County Health Officer Dr. Muntu Davis put the core message simply: "Never touch a bat or any wild animals." The county's rabies guidance asks residents to report any bat found indoors, or any bat outdoors that appears sick, is active during the day, cannot fly, or is dead. Treatment Demand and Costs Are Rising Nationally California's numbers arrive as federal health officials warn of a national increase in human rabies exposures. In a Sept. 10 health advisory, the CDC said it received 17% more rabies-related inquiries in July and August than during the same period a year earlier. Use of rabies vaccines rose an estimated 33%, and use of rabies immune globulin rose 76%. The agency said there is currently no shortage. MedicalDaily covered the advisory's warning about treatment errors. Post-exposure treatment prevents rabies when it is given appropriately before symptoms start, but it is expensive. A typical course costs $11,000 to $14,000 per person, according to the CDC. That is why a risk assessment matters. The CDC says treatment generally is not recommended when the animal can be observed for 10 days, tests negative, or officials determine there was no rabies risk. For bats, testing is often the deciding factor. If it can be done safely, the bat should be contained rather than released so animal control can test it. Local health departments can help families weigh the risk, and patients can ask their insurer how post-exposure treatment is covered. Steps to Take After Finding a Bat at Home Do not touch a bat with bare hands, and keep children and pets away. If someone was bitten or scratched, or a bat's saliva may have reached the eyes, nose, mouth, or a wound, wash the area with soap and water for 15 minutes and contact a clinician or the local health department right away. Bat bites can be tiny, so waking up with a bat in the room or finding one near a sleeping child should be treated as a possible exposure, according to Los Angeles County officials. Keep dogs and cats current on rabies vaccines, including indoor pets, since the county notes that at least one rabid bat is found indoors every year. Seal gaps where bats can get into attics and living spaces. Rabies symptoms in people can take weeks to months to appear and may begin like the flu, with fever and headache, before progressing to neurological problems. Once symptoms start, the disease is almost always fatal, which is why officials urge prompt evaluation instead of waiting. The risk to any one Californian remains low, and the numbers call for vigilance rather than panic. Los Angeles County updates its map as new bats test positive, and MedicalDaily will follow whether the county breaks its 2021 record this fall. Provisional state data count 252 rabid animals from Jan. 1 through Aug. 31, including 232 bats, 19 skunks, and one dog. These are animal cases, not human cases. Why are more rabid bats being found? Officials do not know for certain. Ventura County's animal services said the cause of its increase is unclear, and higher counts can also reflect more bats being found and tested. How many rabid bats has Los Angeles County found? The county had confirmed 66 rabid bats as of its Sept. 21 update, two short of the record 68 set in 2021. About two-thirds were in the Santa Clarita Valley. What counts as a rabies exposure from a bat? A bite, a scratch, or saliva reaching the eyes, nose, mouth, or a wound. Waking up with a bat in the room or finding one near a sleeping child is treated as a possible exposure. What should I do if I find a bat at home? Do not touch it, keep people and pets away, and call animal control. If contact may have occurred, wash the area for 15 minutes and contact a clinician or the health department. Is there a rabies vaccine shortage? No. The CDC said on Sept. 10 that there is currently no shortage of human rabies vaccine or human rabies immune globulin in the United States. analysis_zh.event: 洛杉矶县今年已确认66例狂犬病蝙蝠病例,接近2021年的历史最高纪录68例。截至2026年8月,加州累计报告了252例动物狂犬病病例,其中包括232例蝙蝠、19例浣熊和1例狗。这些均为动物病例,而非人类病例。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 洛杉矶县确认了66例狂犬病蝙蝠病例,加州全省累计报告了252例动物狂犬病病例。家庭面临的风险是接触狂犬病蝙蝠,这可能导致人们需要昂贵的疫苗接种系列,并对未接种疫苗的宠物进行严格的后续处理。2026年的数据是暂定的,可能会有所变化。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 洛杉矶县公共卫生部门已更新其狂犬病地图,加州公共卫生部门提供了暂定数据。风险被强调为与暴露有关,狂犬病蝙蝠报告数量的增加已被注意到,但尚未完全解释。这些记录被描述为类似于家庭检查清单。

Ask complex medical questions and find the latest clinical guidance for drugs & conditions with Medscape AI× EN RegisterLog In AI Mode Medscape News EuropeInternational Approvals EU Panel Recommends New Rabies Vaccine for All Ages Edited by Zeel Mehta September 22, 2026 31 Add to Email Alerts Jump to Key Points At its September 2026 meeting, the European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) adopted a positive opinion recommending marketing authorization for VaxRabeo (rabies vaccine [inactivated] for human use; Sanofi Winthrop Industrie). The recommended indication covers pre-exposure and postexposure prophylaxis against rabies in individuals of all age groups, to be used in accordance with official recommendations. A Potentially Fatal Disease Rabies is one of the most lethal infectious diseases known, with a case fatality rate approaching 100% once clinical symptoms appear, yet it is preventable through timely vaccination. Dog bites account roughly 99% of rabies cases in humans. Protective Antibody Response VaxRabeo is a purified, inactivated rabies vaccine derived from the WISTAR PM/WI38 1503-3M virus strain, supplied as a powder and solvent for suspension for injection. Vaccination induces neutralizing antibodies against the surface glycoprotein of the rabies virus. The CHMP concluded that the vaccine reliably produces a protective antibody response in both adults and children, whether given before exposure, after exposure, or as a booster dose. SUGGESTED FOR YOU Safety Profile In adults, the most frequently reported adverse reactions to VaxRabeo were injection-site pain, myalgia, headache, and malaise. In children, the most common reactions were injection-site pain or swelling and myalgia in those aged 2 years or older, along with abnormal crying and irritability in infants aged 12-23 months. Next Steps The CHMP opinion now goes to the European Commission, which typically issues a final marketing authorization decision within about 67 days. Detailed guidance on administration and dosing schedules will be outlined in the Summary of Product Characteristics, which will be published in all official European Union languages following final authorization by the European Commission. This article was created using several editorial tools, including AI, as part of the process. Human editors reviewed this content before publication. analysis.time: The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) adopted a positive opinion at its September 2026 meeting. The article was published on September 22, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The European Union, covering all age groups of individuals.
analysis.event: The EU Panel (CHMP) recommended marketing authorization for VaxRabeo, a new rabies vaccine for human use, for pre-exposure and postexposure prophylaxis against rabies.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Rabies is a potentially fatal disease with a case fatality rate approaching 100% once clinical symptoms appear. The vaccine is intended to prevent rabies in humans, with no specific case or death counts reported in the supplied evidence.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CHMP opinion is pending final authorization by the European Commission, which typically takes about 67 days. Detailed guidance on administration and dosing schedules will be published in the Summary of Product Characteristics in all official EU languages.

analysis.brief_en: The European Medicines Agency’s Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) has recommended marketing authorization for VaxRabeo, a new rabies vaccine for human use, for pre-exposure and postexposure prophylaxis against rabies in individuals of all age groups. This recommendation was made at the CHMP’s September 2026 meeting and is now awaiting final approval from the European Commission, which typically takes about 67 days. Rabies is a highly lethal infectious disease, with a case fatality rate approaching 100% once symptoms appear, but it is preventable through timely vaccination. The vaccine is derived from the WISTAR PM/WI38 1503-3M virus strain and is supplied as a powder and solvent for suspension for injection. news.content: Sunday, Sep 27, 2026 Search Hyderabad Telangana AP News India World Entertainment Sport Science and Tech Business Rewind ... NRI View Point cartoon My Space Education Today Reviews Property Lifestyle E-Paper NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Vins Bioproducts Marks World Rabies Day With Vaccine Drive In Hyderabad VINS Bioproducts marks World Rabies Day with vaccine drive in Hyderabad VINS Bioproducts marked World Rabies Day in Hyderabad with a rabies awareness initiative, including the handover of anti-rabies vaccines for 200 city dogs and a human chain. Doctors and medical representatives called for greater awareness, vaccination and timely treatment By Telangana Today Published Date - 26 September 2026, 05:19 PM Hyderabad: Reinforcing the fight against rabies through a united public health initiative, VINS Bioproducts Ltd brought together DCP Ch Sirisha of Shadnagar and Future City, senior office-bearers from the national medical fraternity and leading doctors from across India to mark World Rabies Day. The event featured the handover of anti-rabies vaccines for 200 city dogs by Siddarth Daga, Managing Director, VINS Bioproducts, to DCP Ch Sirisha, alongside a Human Chain for Rabies Awareness, highlighting the collective commitment to preventing one of the world’s deadliest yet entirely preventable diseases. Powered By VidCrunch Powered by VidCrunch Next Stay Playback speed 1x Normal Quality Auto Back 322p 240p 144p Auto Back 0.25x 0.5x 1x Normal 1.5x 2x 00:00/01:00 The initiative witnessed the participation of Dr Krishna Kumar Singh, Vice-President, and Dr Hemant Kumar Gohil, Secretary-General, along with zonal representatives from across the country, reflecting a nationwide call for strengthening awareness, vaccination and timely post-exposure treatment, a press release said. Ch Sirisha said the fight against rabies extends beyond healthcare and requires active participation from civic authorities, communities and responsible pet owners. Siddarth Daga said rabies continues to be one of the most preventable yet overlooked public health challenges. NRI View Point cartoon My Space Education Today Reviews Property Lifestyle E-Paper NRI View Point cartoon My Space Reviews Education Today Property Lifestyle Home | Hyderabad | Vins Bioproducts Marks World Rabies Day With Vaccine Drive In Hyderabad VINS Bioproducts marks World Rabies Day with vaccine drive in Hyderabad VINS Bioproducts marked World Rabies Day in Hyderabad with a rabies awareness initiative, including the handover of anti-rabies vaccines for 200 city dogs and a human chain. Doctors and medical representatives called for greater awareness, vaccination and timely treatment By Telangana Today Published Date - 26 September 2026, 05:19 PM Hyderabad: Reinforcing the fight against rabies through a united public health initiative, VINS Bioproducts Ltd brought together DCP Ch Sirisha of Shadnagar and Future City, senior office-bearers from the national medical fraternity and leading doctors from across India to mark World Rabies Day. The event featured the handover of anti-rabies vaccines for 200 city dogs by Siddarth Daga, Managing Director, VINS Bioproducts, to DCP Ch Sirisha, alongside a Human Chain for Rabies Awareness, highlighting the collective commitment to preventing one of the world’s deadliest yet entirely preventable diseases. Powered By VidCrunch Powered by VidCrunch Next Stay Playback speed 1x Normal Quality Auto Back 322p 240p 144p Auto Back 0.25x 0.5x 1x Normal 1.5x 2x 00:00/01:00 The initiative witnessed the participation of Dr Krishna Kumar Singh, Vice-President, and Dr Hemant Kumar Gohil, Secretary-General, along with zonal representatives from across the country, reflecting a nationwide call for strengthening awareness, vaccination and timely post-exposure treatment, a press release said. Ch Sirisha said the fight against rabies extends beyond healthcare and requires active participation from civic authorities, communities and responsible pet owners. Siddarth Daga said rabies continues to be one of the most preventable yet overlooked public health challenges. news.content_zh: 2026年9月27日,VINS Bioproducts 在海得拉巴-泰伦加纳州组织了一项 狂犬病 意识活动,作为世界 狂犬病 日的一部分。活动包括向200只城市犬分发抗 狂犬病 疫苗 药物,并组织人链以强调集体承诺预防 狂犬病,这是一种完全可预防但仍是全球致命性疾病之一。该活动与市政当局、医疗代表和社区成员合作,反映了全国范围内呼吁提高意识和 疫苗接种 的努力。活动在2026年9月26日发布的新闻稿中被强调为一项公共卫生运动。未报告具体病例数或死亡人数,但此次活动突出了及时进行暴露后 治疗 的重要性以及社区在对抗 狂犬病 中的作用。

Is Your Pet Safe? Mary Simpson Thu, September 24, 2026 at 7:05 PM UTC 3 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Once upon a time, this dread virus was practically eradicated in North America. Not anymore. But it's easy to keep your pet safe. rabies is back is your pet safe, photo credit Jack Bulmer shutterstock com For all pet parents, caring for our four-legged fur kids typically includes providing top-quality food, an active lifestyle, and the appropriate round of vaccines each year. But while all these steps are fairly rote for many of us, that last one has become critical. You see, health officials are now reinforcing to pet owners the importance of staying on top of those rabies vaccines. Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yes, several states are not only reporting that animals have tested positive for rabies but that they're experiencing sharp increases in these types of incidents over previous years. In fact, for the lone-star state of Texas, they're dealing with their first reported cases in over a decade and that includes 22 separate incidences of rabies in wild animals. While the world's leading health care provider, the Mayo Clinic, has identified the most common carrier of rabies to be bats, they're also flagging foxes, raccoons, skunks, and coyotes as transmitters of the disease. You know... the animals our pets are most likely to come into contact with. And it doesn't require your pet to get into a full-on brawl with an infected critter. A simple scratch or bite where saliva from the rabid animal enters a break in your pet's skin or even finds its way into their eyes, nostrils, or mouth can be enough to infect them. For those of us who have suffered the dread spray of a skunk, the answer is "no", your dog can't get rabies from being sprayed. Symptoms will typically show up three to eight weeks after your pet has been exposed to the virus and include extreme agitation, drooling, dilated pupils, and an inability to swallow. Unfortunately, once the signs present themselves, the condition is always 100% fatal as the virus infects the central nervous system. Advertisement Advertisement If your pet has been bitten by an animal you suspect may be rabid, get them to the emergency vet immediately. If they are up-to-date on their vaccines, a booster shot will be administered. Your pet will then need to be quarantined to watch for any change in behavior. If they are already showing signs of toxicity, euthanasia will be recommended as the life expectancy is somewhere in the range of seven to 10 days. Now, for those new to dog ownership, here's how the rabies vaccine works. If you adopt a puppy, they will get their first shot when they're between three and four months of age. That will be good for one year. After a year, they get a booster to help build up their immune system. Following that, you should have your pet immunized every one to three years. Check your state or provincial requirements, because they may vary, however your veterinarian will be able to send you reminders as the required reimmunization date comes due. Above all else, don't ever think you can skip a year because your pet is primarily indoors and safe from wildlife. An assumption like that can cost them their life. news.title_zh: 狂犬病卷土重来!您的宠物安全吗?
news.source_body_en: Rabies has seen a resurgence in several U.S. states, with Texas reporting its first cases in over a decade, totaling 22 incidents in wild animals. Health officials are urging pet owners to prioritize rabies vaccinations for their pets, as the virus can be transmitted through scratches or bites from infected wildlife. Once symptoms appear, rabies is always fatal, and pets showing signs may require euthanasia. The article emphasizes the importance of staying on top of vaccine schedules, even for indoor pets, and recommends immediate veterinary attention if exposure is suspected. While the article does not provide specific case or death counts, it highlights the growing concern over rabies in North America and the need for vigilance among pet owners.

Updated: September 26, 2026 @ 6:59 pm Full Forecast Watch Live Watch Pastor Ricky Floyd's Homegoing Ceremony Live Weather News Your Money FOX13 Investigates Your Health ONLY ON FOX13 ELECTION 2026 Share This Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email News Featured CDC warns of increase in potential rabies exposures: What Mid-South doctors say you need to know Mandy Hrach Mandy Hrach FOX13 Memphis Health Reporter Author facebook Author twitter Author email Sep 24, 2026 Sep 24, 2026 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email WATCH: CDC warns of increase in potential rabies exposures: What Mid-South doctors say you need to know Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save MEMPHIS, Tenn. - Health officials are urging people to know what to do after a possible rabies exposure as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports an increase in encounters with rabid or potentially rabid animals in parts of the country. Doctors and veterinarians stress the warning does not necessarily mean rabies itself is becoming more common or cases are rising. Instead, it highlights the importance of recognizing a possible exposure and getting treatment when needed. “There’ve been some increased encounters with animals that can carry rabies,” infectious disease specialist Dr. Steve Threlkeld said. “And the problem with rabies, of course, is that it is essentially 100% fatal.” The CDC said multiple jurisdictions have reported increases in human exposures to rabid or potentially rabid animals since July. Dr. Thomas Slattery, a veterinarian at Walnut Grove Animal Clinic in Memphis, said that does not necessarily indicate an increase in animal rabies cases. “It does not mean that animal cases are on the rise,” Dr. Slattery said. “But it does mean that we’re doing a better job of recognizing exposure and doing the post-exposure prophylaxis.” Bats are a common source of rabies exposure in the United States, and their bites can be small enough that someone may not realize they have been bitten. “There’ll be a bat flying around in a room in a house,” Dr. Threlkeld said. “If it’s flying in a bedroom where people have been asleep, you will never know whether that bat has bitten you.” Dr. Threlkeld said skunks are also a significant concern in the Mid-South, followed by raccoons and foxes. Pets can encounter those animals without their owners witnessing what happened. “It would be an interaction with one of those animals that could happen without the dog even knowing,” Dr. Slattery said. “Or it could happen without anybody ever seeing what happened.” Rabies is primarily spread when saliva from an infected animal enters the body, typically through a bite. Dr. Slattery said scratches can also be concerning if saliva is present on an animal’s claws. If a dog or cat may have been exposed, Dr. Slattery recommends contacting a veterinarian. If the pet has an open wound, owners should wear gloves when handling the animal. Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies is one of the most important ways to protect them. “The number one thing is vaccination," Dr. Slattery said. Despite the seriousness of the disease, human rabies is extremely rare in the United States. Dr. Threlkeld said Tennessee has not recorded a human rabies case since 2002, and only a small number of human cases typically occur nationwide each year. But rabies is particularly dangerous because once symptoms begin, the disease is nearly always fatal. Symptoms may not appear immediately. Dr. Threlkeld said they can develop weeks or even months after an exposure, making it possible for someone to no longer connect their illness to an earlier animal encounter. That is why treatment after a potential exposure is critical. For someone who has not previously been vaccinated against rabies, CDC guidance calls for immediate wound care, a dose of human rabies immune globulin, and a four-dose rabies vaccine series given over two weeks. “Don’t delay,” Dr. Threlkeld said. “You need the vaccine because once symptoms start, it’s too late. A vaccine does not help, and it is nearly 100% fatal.” Anyone who believes they may have been exposed to rabies should contact a health care provider or local health department for guidance. Pet owners who believe their animal may have been exposed should contact a veterinarian. Download the FOX13 Memphis app to receive alerts from breaking news in your neighborhood. Updated: September 26, 2026 @ 6:59 pm Full Forecast Watch Live Watch Pastor Ricky Floyd's Homegoing Ceremony Live Weather News Your Money FOX13 Investigates Your Health ONLY ON FOX13 ELECTION 2026 Share This Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email News Featured CDC warns of increase in potential rabies exposures: What Mid-South doctors say you need to know Mandy Hrach Mandy Hrach FOX13 Memphis Health Reporter Author facebook Author twitter Author email Sep 24, 2026 Sep 24, 2026 Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email WATCH: CDC warns of increase in potential rabies exposures: What Mid-South doctors say you need to know Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Copy article link Save MEMPHIS, Tenn. - Health officials are urging people to know what to do after a possible rabies exposure as the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reports an increase in encounters with rabid or potentially rabid animals in parts of the country. Doctors and veterinarians stress the warning does not necessarily mean rabies itself is becoming more common or cases are rising. Instead, it highlights the importance of recognizing a possible exposure and getting treatment when needed. “There’ve been some increased encounters with animals that can carry rabies,” infectious disease specialist Dr. Steve Threlkeld said. “And the problem with rabies, of course, is that it is essentially 100% fatal.” The CDC said multiple jurisdictions have reported increases in human exposures to rabid or potentially rabid animals since July. Dr. Thomas Slattery, a veterinarian at Walnut Grove Animal Clinic in Memphis, said that does not necessarily indicate an increase in animal rabies cases. “It does not mean that animal cases are on the rise,” Dr. Slattery said. “But it does mean that we’re doing a better job of recognizing exposure and doing the post-exposure prophylaxis.” Bats are a common source of rabies exposure in the United States, and their bites can be small enough that someone may not realize they have been bitten. “There’ll be a bat flying around in a room in a house,” Dr. Threlkeld said. “If it’s flying in a bedroom where people have been asleep, you will never know whether that bat has bitten you.” Dr. Threlkeld said skunks are also a significant concern in the Mid-South, followed by raccoons and foxes. Pets can encounter those animals without their owners witnessing what happened. “It would be an interaction with one of those animals that could happen without the dog even knowing,” Dr. Slattery said. “Or it could happen without anybody ever seeing what happened.” Rabies is primarily spread when saliva from an infected animal enters the body, typically through a bite. Dr. Slattery said scratches can also be concerning if saliva is present on an animal’s claws. If a dog or cat may have been exposed, Dr. Slattery recommends contacting a veterinarian. If the pet has an open wound, owners should wear gloves when handling the animal. Keeping pets vaccinated against rabies is one of the most important ways to protect them. “The number one thing is vaccination," Dr. Slattery said. Despite the seriousness of the disease, human rabies is extremely rare in the United States. Dr. Threlkeld said Tennessee has not recorded a human rabies case since 2002, and only a small number of human cases typically occur nationwide each year. But rabies is particularly dangerous because once symptoms begin, the disease is nearly always fatal. Symptoms may not appear immediately. Dr. Threlkeld said they can develop weeks or even months after an exposure, making it possible for someone to no longer connect their illness to an earlier animal encounter. That is why treatment after a potential exposure is critical. For someone who has not previously been vaccinated against rabies, CDC guidance calls for immediate wound care, a dose of human rabies immune globulin, and a four-dose rabies vaccine series given over two weeks. “Don’t delay,” Dr. Threlkeld said. “You need the vaccine because once symptoms start, it’s too late. A vaccine does not help, and it is nearly 100% fatal.” Anyone who believes they may have been exposed to rabies should contact a health care provider or local health department for guidance. Pet owners who believe their animal may have been exposed should contact a veterinarian. Download the FOX13 Memphis app to receive alerts from breaking news in your neighborhood. news.content: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC) has issued a health advisory as a response to recent reports of increases in human exposure to rabid or possible rabid animals. Locally, two bats collected across the county have tested positive for rabies, according to the Niagara County health department. The bats were captured on Sept. 14 in Niagara Falls and Sept. 15 in the Town of Lockport. They were confirmed rabid by the state Department of Health Wadsworth Center on Thursday. There have been several reports of rabid bats in Niagara County this summer. Rabies in animals remains a significant public health concern in Niagara County. Rabies is a viral disease that is almost always fatal to unvaccinated animals. Anyone who may have had potential contact with a bat should immediately contact their local health department to ensure prompt investigation of any human or domestic pet exposure. Bats, raccoons, skunks, and foxes are common wildlife carriers of the rabies virus. A rabid animal can shed the virus through direct contact even before symptoms appear. Laboratory testing is the only way to confirm rabies in an animal. The CDC issued the health alert Thursday after seeing an uptick in the exposures as well as rabies post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) administration errors. Since July 2026, multiple United States jurisdictions have reported local increases in human rabies exposures involving known rabies vectors or animals in which rabies is less commonly reported, the CDC reported. "Several high-profile rabies outbreaks and mass rabies exposure events have highlighted the importance of performing careful rabies risk assessments and following evidence-based recommendations for administering PEP," the CDC stated. "Health departments can help clinicians who provide rabies vaccination in their jurisdictions stay aware of the importance of rabies risk assessments before administering PEP." Rabies is nearly 100% fatal if left untreated, but can be preventable if the person exposed is given post-exposure prophylaxis treatment early enough, the CDC reported. An infected animal can spread rabies to humans and other animals through bites, scratches, or oral secretions. Rabies primarily affects the central nervous system, leading to encephalitis and death if medical care is not received soon after exposure and before symptoms start. The CDC reported that it received 17% more rabies inquiries from July through August 2025 than during the same period in 2025, including reports of mass exposure events involving more than one person. During this time frame, CDC also received reports from at least eight state health departments of increased rabies PEP use, PEP administration errors, or both, the CDC reported. An estimated 1.4 million people in the United States seek medical care after animal contact and undergo evaluation each year, and approximately 100,000 people receive rabies PEP following a potential exposure. According to weekly pharmacy data as of September 2, 2026, utilization for the two rabies vaccines and the two rabies immunoglobulins licensed in the United States has increased by an estimated 33% and 76%, respectively, compared with the same time period last year, the CDC stated. For further information on rabies or to report an animal bite or contact with wild animals, please call the Niagara County Department of Health Environmental Division at 716-439-7444 or visit www.niagaracounty.gov/rabies . Natasha Vaughn-Holdridge from the Post-Star in Glens Falls contributed to this report. Rabies is nearly 100% fatal if untreated but can be preventable with early PEP. The CDC is urging health departments to ensure clinicians perform risk assessments before administering PEP, emphasizing that laboratory testing is the only way to confirm rabies in animals. The Niagara County Department of Health Environmental Division is available for further information or reports of animal bites.

news.content: asian games 2026cec gyanesh kumarelection commissiontata trusts ❯ E हिं অ বাং ગુ ಕ മ म ଓ ਪੰ த తె ار ❯ National English हिंदी उत्तर प्रदेशउत्तराखंडछत्तीसगढ़झारखंडदिल्लीबिहारमध्य प्रदेशराजस्थानहरियाणाहिमाचल प्रदेश অসমীয়া বাংলা ગુજરાતી ಕನ್ನಡ മലയാളം मराठी ଓଡିଆ ਪੰਜਾਬੀ தமிழ் తెలుగు ఆంధ్రప్రదేశ్తెలంగాణ اردو Live NATIONAL WORLD SPORTS ENTERTAINMENT OPINION PHOTOS HEALTH STATE BUSINESS More Live ETV Bharat / state Fake Drug Racket Busted In Delhi; 481 Units Of Counterfeit Rabies Vaccine Seized Officials secured 120 vials for testing and seized the remaining stock and seven purchase invoices under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act. Representational Image (IANS) By ETV Bharat English Team Published : September 23, 2026 at 12:07 PM IST 2 Min Read New Delhi: A major fake drug racket, allegedly putting people's lives at risk, has been busted in Delhi. The Delhi Drugs Control Department raided a firm in Bhagirath Palace and seized 481 units of counterfeit rabies vaccine worth around Rs 2 lakh. The case has links to Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, triggering concern in the health department. Taking serious note of the matter, Delhi Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh has strongly reacted to the seizure. He made it clear that the government's policy is "zero tolerance" for those selling fake and adulterated medicines. The Health Minister said, "Rabies is a very serious and, in many cases, fatal disease. Therefore, no compromise with the quality or safety of rabies vaccines will be tolerated. Strict legal action will be taken against those involved in this illegal trade under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940." Raids Conducted On Three Bhagirath Palace Premises Acting on a tip-off and directions from the Delhi Drugs Control Department, a special team conducted an extensive search operation on three premises in Bhagirath Palace, one of the capital's major medicine markets. During the operation, the team recovered 481 counterfeit units of "Rabies Vaccine, Human I P (Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine) - (Abhayrab)" from a sales premises and a warehouse. After verifying the matter with the original manufacturer, M/S Human Biological Institute, Telangana, the company confirmed that it had not issued the recovered vaccine batch and that it was completely counterfeit. Illegal Network Traced To Kanpur The Drugs Control Department team secured 120 vials as samples for testing. The team seized the remaining 361 vaccine units, along with seven purchase invoices, under Sections 22(1)(C) and 22(1)(CC) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. All samples have been sent to the CRI Centre in Kasauli for quality testing and analysis. During the investigation, the Bhagirath Palace firm revealed that it had purchased the counterfeit vaccine from an agency in Kanpur. Following this crucial lead, the Delhi Drugs Control Department immediately shared the information with the Uttar Pradesh Drugs Control Department. Based on the information, the UP team raided two locations in Kanpur, where the agency admitted to supplying the counterfeit vaccine to Delhi. Delhi Health Minister said the department was working to uncover the entire syndicate. Authorities are trying to identify the alleged kingpin behind the counterfeit drug network, the source of the medicines and the distribution chain. The Delhi Drugs Control Department has made it clear that those responsible will not be spared and that the law will be strictly enforced. Representational Image (IANS) By ETV Bharat English Team Published : September 23, 2026 at 12:07 PM IST 2 Min Read New Delhi: A major fake drug racket, allegedly putting people's lives at risk, has been busted in Delhi. The Delhi Drugs Control Department raided a firm in Bhagirath Palace and seized 481 units of counterfeit rabies vaccine worth around Rs 2 lakh. The case has links to Kanpur in Uttar Pradesh, triggering concern in the health department. Taking serious note of the matter, Delhi Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh has strongly reacted to the seizure. He made it clear that the government's policy is "zero tolerance" for those selling fake and adulterated medicines. The Health Minister said, "Rabies is a very serious and, in many cases, fatal disease. Therefore, no compromise with the quality or safety of rabies vaccines will be tolerated. Strict legal action will be taken against those involved in this illegal trade under the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940." Raids Conducted On Three Bhagirath Palace Premises Acting on a tip-off and directions from the Delhi Drugs Control Department, a special team conducted an extensive search operation on three premises in Bhagirath Palace, one of the capital's major medicine markets. During the operation, the team recovered 481 counterfeit units of "Rabies Vaccine, Human I P (Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine) - (Abhayrab)" from a sales premises and a warehouse. After verifying the matter with the original manufacturer, M/S Human Biological Institute, Telangana, the company confirmed that it had not issued the recovered vaccine batch and that it was completely counterfeit. Illegal Network Traced To Kanpur The Drugs Control Department team secured 120 vials as samples for testing. The team seized the remaining 361 vaccine units, along with seven purchase invoices, under Sections 22(1)(C) and 22(1)(CC) of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940. All samples have been sent to the CRI Centre in Kasauli for quality testing and analysis. During the investigation, the Bhagirath Palace firm revealed that it had purchased the counterfeit vaccine from an agency in Kanpur. Following this crucial lead, the Delhi Drugs Control Department immediately shared the information with the Uttar Pradesh Drugs Control Department. Based on the information, the UP team raided two locations in Kanpur, where the agency admitted to supplying the counterfeit vaccine to Delhi. Delhi Health Minister said the department was working to uncover the entire syndicate. Authorities are trying to identify the alleged kingpin behind the counterfeit drug network, the source of the medicines and the distribution chain. The Delhi Drugs Control Department has made it clear that those responsible will not be spared and that the law will be strictly enforced. news.content: Sep. 23—A bat found in Lewis County has tested positive for rabies virus at the Washington Public Health Laboratories, according to a news release from Lewis County Public Health and Social Services. Additional information, including where the bat was found, was not provided in the news release. "To protect yourself and your family from rabies, it's important to avoid touching bats or other wildlife, and to contact your healthcare provider and Lewis County Public Health & Social Services if you or someone you know has had contact with a bat or potentially rabid animal," the news release states. "Rabies is a fatal disease in both people and animals, but it can be prevented with prompt, appropriate medical care and treatment before any symptoms develop." In Washington state, bats are the only known mammal to carry rabies, according to the news release. "Washington state is home to many bats, the majority of which are healthy and vital to our ecosystem. Only a small portion of bats carry rabies virus," the news release stated. "However, other mammals, including people, can get rabies from bats. Rabies virus is found in an infected animal's saliva and brain tissue. It is usually spread to people by animal bites or scratches. The county provided tips to prevent rabies: —Do not touch or handle bats or other wild animals. —Do not touch or handle bats or other wild animals, even if they are dead. Teach children not to touch or handle bats or other wild animals. —Have children tell an adult if they find a bat at home, at school or with a pet. —Keep bats out of your living space by bat-proofing your home (humanely excluding bats). The Washington State Department of Fish and Wildlife provides more information on how to keep bats out of your home. —If you find a bat in your living space, call Lewis County Public Health & Social Services at 360- 740-1223 so that they can help determine if the bat needs to be tested for rabies. —Never handle a bat with bare hands and only capture bats that have had direct contact with a person or pet, or bats found in the room with a person or pet who may have had contact with it. Public Health will advise you on how to safely capture a bat if it needs to be tested for rabies. If you or anyone in your family were bitten by a bat or other animal or had direct contact with a bat or other potentially rabid animal: —Wash out the area of any animal bite or scratch with soap and running water for at least 10 minutes. A bat's teeth and claws are very small, and their bites or scratches may not be visible. —Call Lewis County Public Health and Social Services if you have had any direct contact with a bat or other potentially rabid animal or were bitten or scratched by a potentially rabid animal to discuss the potential for rabies exposure and the need for treatment. —Seek medical care right away for a bite or scratch from a bat or other potentially rabid animal. Rabies can be prevented with appropriate and timely medical treatment, called rabies post-exposure prophylaxis, after a rabies exposure. If your pet has contact with a bat, contact your veterinarian immediately. Dogs, cats, ferrets and horses will need to be revaccinated if they could have been exposed to rabies virus. Protect your pets by getting them vaccinated against rabies on a schedule recommended by a veterinarian. Dogs, cats and ferrets are required to be up to date on rabies vaccination in Washington. Contact Public Health at 360-740-1223 with any questions. Do not bring bats or other animals to Lewis County Public Health and Social Services unless advised to do so by public health staff.
